timeline.text: I have grown old, and my time is near. Send me a boy, so I can teach him magic.
But the boy the king sent him… would bring about the very thing that king feared most.
Among the people who came before you, there was a king. And this king had a sorcerer.
When the sorcerer grew old, the king sent him a boy.
On the road between the king and the sorcerer, there was a monk. One day the boy stopped and listened to him… and he liked what he heard. So every day, he stopped again.
But it made him late. The sorcerer beat him and asked:
What kept you?
And at home, his family beat him and asked the same thing.
The boy told the monk, and the monk said:
When the sorcerer wants to beat you, say: my family kept me. And when your family wants to beat you, say: the sorcerer kept me.
But one day, on that same road… something blocked his way. Something so huge that no one could get past it.
It was a huge, terrifying beast, holding back everyone on the road.
The boy looked at it, and said to himself:
Today I will know which is dearer to Allah: the way of the sorcerer, or the way of the monk.
He picked up a stone, and said:
O Allah, if the way of the monk is dearer to You and more pleasing to You than the way of the sorcerer, then kill this beast, so the people can pass.
He threw the stone… and the beast fell dead.
And the people went on their way.
The boy went to the monk and told him what had happened. The monk said:
My son, you are better than me. You will be tested. And if you are tested, do not lead them to me.
And that stone was only the beginning.
From that day on, the boy would heal the blind, the leper, and people with every kind of illness. And Allah cured them at his hands.
Now the king had a companion who used to sit with him, and he had gone blind. He heard about the boy, and came to him with many gifts. He said:
Heal me, and all of this is yours.
The boy said:
I don't heal anyone. Only Allah heals. If you believe in Allah, I will pray to Him, and He will heal you.
The man believed. The boy prayed. And Allah gave him back his sight.
But then the man went back to the king, and sat beside him, just as he always had. And the king had one question for him.
The king asked him:
Who gave you back your sight?
He said:
My Lord.
The king said:
Me?
He answered:
No. My Lord, and your Lord, is Allah.
The king asked:
You have a lord other than me?
And he said:
Yes. My Lord and your Lord is Allah.
The king kept torturing him… until he led them to the boy.
The boy was brought in. The king said to him:
My son, has your magic become so great that you heal the blind, and the leper, and all these illnesses?
The king thought it was the very magic he had sent him to learn.
The boy said:
I don't heal anyone. Only Allah heals.
And when the king pressed him, the boy gave the very same answer:
My Lord and your Lord is Allah.
So the king took him and tortured him too… until he led them to the monk.
The monk was brought. The king said to him:
Turn back from your religion.
He refused. And he was killed.
Then the king said to his companion:
Turn back from your religion.
He refused. And he was killed too.
Now only one of them was left.
The boy.
The king said to the boy:
Turn back from your religion.
The boy refused.
So the king sent him off with a group of his men. He told them:
Take him to that mountain. When you reach the top, if he turns back from his religion, let him be. If not, throw him off.
They climbed, higher and higher, until they reached the top.
And the boy said:
O Allah, deal with them for me, however You will.
The mountain shook.
And the men tumbled down from it. Every one of them.
And the boy came walking back… until he stood in front of the king.
The king asked:
What happened to the men who were with you?
The boy said:
Allah dealt with them for me.
So the king tried again. This time… he sent him out to sea.
The king sent him off with another group of men, and said:
Take him out in a small boat. When you reach the middle of the sea, if he turns back from his religion, let him be. If not, drown him.
They took him out, far into the deep sea.
And again the boy said:
O Allah, deal with them for me, however You will.
The boat turned over… and they drowned. Every one of them.
And once again, the boy came back to the king.
The king asked:
What happened to the men who were with you?
And the boy said:
Allah dealt with them for me.
Twice the king's men had died. Twice the boy had walked back alive.
Then the boy said something the king never expected.
He said:
You will not kill me until you do what I tell you. If you do it, you will kill me. If you don't, you never can.
The king asked:
And what is that?
The boy said:
Gather all the people on one open plain. Tie me to the trunk of a tree. Then take an arrow from my own quiver, and say: In the name of Allah, the Lord of the boy. If you do that, you will kill me.
So the king did it.
The people were gathered on one plain. The boy was tied to the trunk of a tree.
The king took an arrow from the boy's quiver, set it in the middle of the bow… and said:
In the name of Allah, the Lord of the boy.
In front of all the people.
Then he shot.
The arrow struck him on the temple. The boy put his hand where it had struck… and he died.
And the people cried out:
Someone came to the king and said: "Do you see what you were afraid of? By Allah, it has come down on you. All the people have believed."
The king had killed the boy. But he had lost the people.
So the king gave an order…
Trenches were dug at the mouths of the roads. And fires were lit inside them.
Then the king said:
Whoever turns back from his religion, let him go. Whoever doesn't, throw him in.
And the believers went forward, one after another, pressing toward it.
A woman came, holding her baby son, a child she was still nursing.
But she seemed to hold back from the fire.
Then her baby spoke. He said: "Be patient, mother. You are on the truth."
The king had asked one question:
A man who had been blind. A monk. A boy. And then the people themselves. They kept firm.
